妄.meaning: A <part>woman</part> buys an old cottage with a mossy, nameless <part>tombstone</part> in the garden and decides it's a doorway to fairyland. Every night she knocks on it, asks for tea, and swears a fairy pours her a cup. Nobody is there: it's a cosy <kanji>delusion</kanji>.
妄.on: Every Sunday she trims round it with a tiny lawn <sound>mow</sound>er, so the fairies won't trip.
妄.kun: '<sound>Me</sound>? Drink your tea without asking?' she scolds a <sound>du</sound>ck that waddles in and helps itself.

腫.meaning: The <part>moon</part> bumps into a mountain top one night and wakes with a lump so <part>heavy</part> it tips sideways in the sky. Astronomers point every telescope at the new bulge. An old star doctor takes a look and says it's just a harmless <kanji>tumor</kanji>.
腫.on: She prescribes one <sound>su</sound>gar cube a night to cheer the moon up.
腫.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the sun, until its own nose starts to swell.

肪.meaning: The <part>moon</part> eats so many midnight snacks that it grows too round to float, and sailors have to tie a <part>sail</part> to it so the wind can drag it across the sky. Each month it's a little rounder. The star doctors agree: the moon is <kanji>obese</kanji>.
肪.on: When the sail slips, it rolls across the sea like a giant <sound>bou</sound>lder.

粧.meaning: Behind a garden <part>shed</part>, a scarecrow wants to look its best for the harvest fair. It powders its face with crushed <part>rice</part> and rubs red <part>soil</part> on its cheeks for blush. The crows have never seen it so pretty: homemade <kanji>cosmetics</kanji>.
粧.on: It wins first prize at the fair's scarecrow beauty <sound>show</sound>.

茂.meaning: A knight leaves his <part>battle axe</part> lying in a meadow for one summer. When he comes back, the <part>grass</part> has swallowed it: only the shiny blade pokes up from a jungle of weeds taller than his horse. The whole field is <kanji>overgrown</kanji>.
茂.on: Even the axe handle has turned furry with green <sound>mo</sound>ss.
茂.kun: '<sound>She</sound> <sound>ge</sound>ts it out first!' shouts his little sister, diving into the weeds.

寧.meaning: Under his cosy <part>roof</part>, an old fisherman mends his <part>net</part> by the window while a noisy parade marches down the <part>street</part> outside. Friends bang on the door, but his <part>heart</part> is calm. Join the crowd? He'd <kanji>rather</kanji> not.
寧.on: A parade horse gives a loud <sound>nei</sound>gh at his window, but he doesn't look up.
寧.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se dressed as a <sound>shee</sound>p peeks in too, then decides it would rather nap by his stove.

髄.meaning: A dinosaur <part>skeleton</part> is wheeled down the museum's loading <part>ramp</part>, and a leg bone cracks open. Inside is a soft, glowing core the old giant still seems to <part>possess</part>, like jam in a doughnut. The scientists gasp: real <kanji>marrow</kanji>.
髄.on: It smells faintly of a yu<sound>zu</sound>-glazed <sound>ee</sound>l, which nobody can explain.

逮.meaning: A cleaner is washing a skate <part>ramp</part> when a thief with a stolen handbag whizzes down it on a skateboard. She sticks out her <part>mop</part>, tangles his wheels and sits on him until the police arrive. She's the first cleaner in town to <kanji>apprehend</kanji> a thief.
逮.on: She ties his hands behind him with his own <sound>tie</sound>.

鹿.meaning: One snowy night, a shy visitor sneaks into a garden <part>shed</part> and licks the honey off <part>two spoons</part> left on the bench. In the morning the farmer finds hoofprints in the snow and antler scratches on the rafters. The thief was a <kanji>deer</kanji>.
鹿.on: When he opens the door the next night, it shoots out like a <sound>roc</sound>ket.
鹿.kun: '<sound>She</sound>'ll be back,' he tells his wife, staying very <sound>ca</sound>lm so he won't scare her off.

麗.meaning: A painter nails <part>one</part> plank across two empty picture <part>frame</part> shapes in a forest clearing and waits. A <part>deer</part> steps beneath them, and its antlers poke up through the frames just right. She paints it before it moves: the most <kanji>lovely</kanji> portrait of her life.
麗.on: Overhead, a kite shaped like a <sound>ray</sound> glides past, and she paints that in too.
麗.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>h!' sigh the gallery visitors at the <sound>ru</sound>by sunset behind the deer, nibbling <sound>wa</sound>sabi peas.

妬.meaning: A <part>woman</part> keeps a smooth <part>stone</part> on her windowsill, and her cat adores it more than her: it sleeps on the stone, purrs at the stone, and brings the stone its toys. She glares at the rock, red in the face and wildly <kanji>jealous</kanji>.
妬.on: She carves the cat's face on a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, hoping to win it back.
妬.kun: She hides the stone in a <sound>ne</sound>t with a <sound>ta</sound>co for bait, but the cat drags it home anyway.

陵.meaning: On a hill of <part>soil</part>, a royal <part>pennant</part> flutters above the tomb of a long-dead king. A guard on a <part>folding chair</part> dozes by its stone door, his <part>legs</part> stretched across the path. Tourists tiptoe over him to enter the <kanji>mausoleum</kanji>.
陵.on: They spend the night in a <sound>ryo</sound>kan at the foot of the hill to see the tomb at dawn.
陵.kun: '<sound>Me</sound> next,' says a lady in a <sound>sa</sound>ri, tossing <sound>sa</sound>rdines to the <sound>gee</sound>se on the hill.

楼.meaning: A <part>rice carrier</part> balances her bundle on her head and climbs a lone <part>tree</part> to watch for thieves in the paddies. She nails planks up there, adds a roof and a ladder, and stays all harvest. Soon the village calls it the <kanji>watchtower</kanji>.
楼.on: She grows one red <sound>ro</sound>se in a pot on the top platform.
楼.kun: She drops her <sound>ta</sound>co, stays <sound>ca</sound>lm, and a <sound>do</sound>ctor below catches it, sighing '<sound>No</sound>t again!'

摩.meaning: At the village fair, Granny wins the tug-of-war on a thick <part>hemp</part> rope, but her <part>hand</part> is red where the rough fibres rubbed back and forth. She shows off the mark like a medal. Hemp rope will always <kanji>chafe</kanji>.
摩.on: She cools her palm in a <sound>mu</sound>g of cold milk.
摩.kun: Her friend rubs on a cream that smells of <sound>sa</sound>rdine and <sound>su</sound>shi.

閑.meaning: A <part>tree</part> grows right between the doors of an old castle <part>gate</part>, so the gate can never shut and nobody needs to guard it. The retired guard ties a hammock to the trunk and swings there all day with a book. Pure <kanji>leisure</kanji>.
閑.on: He wears a pink <sound>carn</sound>ation behind one ear.

栓.meaning: A giant's bathtub keeps draining, so she pulls up a <part>whole</part> <part>tree</part> and jams it, roots first, into the hole. The tub fills, and the leaves float on top like bubbles. It's the best <kanji>plug</kanji> she's ever had.
栓.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try stands beside the tub so nobody pulls it out mid-bath.

彰.meaning: A cat pins a sheriff's <part>badge</part> to its chest and swears it's been on patrol all night. But there's cream on its <part>whiskers</part>, and the fridge door is wide open. Who raided it is plain as day, utterly <kanji>patent</kanji>.
彰.on: The other cats laugh through the whole <sound>show</sound> of its trial.

褐.meaning: A rusty <part>weathervane</part> rooster on a barn complains about the heat, so the farmer fixes a tiny <part>sunshade</part> above it. Too late: years of summer have already baked the metal bird from shiny gold to dull <kanji>brown</kanji>.
褐.on: It's now the exact colour of the crispy <sound>katsu</sound> on the farmer's lunch plate.

娠.meaning: A <part>woman</part> on the beach opens a <part>clam</part> and finds a pearl growing inside. She laughs and pats her round belly: 'You too, little one?' Both of them are carrying something precious: she is <kanji>with child</kanji>.
娠.on: The baby kicks so hard she feels it all the way down in her <sound>shin</sound>.

墳.meaning: Archaeologists dig into a grassy mound of <part>soil</part>, and a hot <part>geyser</part> blasts out, spraying them with steam and old gold coins. Beneath the hill lies a sleeping king on a stone bed: an ancient <kanji>tomb</kanji>.
墳.on: The steam whirls up like a little ty<sound>phoon</sound> and blows their hats away.

挫.meaning: A boat crew drops its <part>anchor</part> and it lands right on a riverside <part>picnic</part>, squashing the cake, the grapes and the lemonade flat. The picnickers stare at the mess. All their plans, gone in one <kanji>crush</kanji>.
挫.on: To say sorry, the crew lets them pick anything from the ship's floating ba<sound>za</sound>ar.
挫.kun: The ship's <sound>coo</sound>k leaps ashore to help and sprains his ankle on a <sound>jee</sound>p's bumper.

舶.meaning: A fisherman paints his tiny rowing <part>boat</part> bright <part>white</part>, adds a paper funnel and six cardboard decks, and tells tourists it's a cruise ship. They pile in anyway. It's the smallest ocean <kanji>liner</kanji> afloat.
舶.on: The only food on the menu is <sound>huck</sound>leberry jam on toast.

骸.meaning: A circus <part>acrobat</part> needs a partner who never gets dizzy, so she trains with an old classroom <part>skeleton</part>. She flips it, spins it and catches it by one ankle. Only one <kanji>bone</kanji> ever falls off: a little toe.
骸.on: A <sound>gui</sound>de dog in the front row fetches the toe and brings it back.
骸.kun: Next on stage: a <sound>moo</sound>se, its <sound>coo</sound>k, and a <sound>ro</sound>cket that fires them both through a hoop.

堕.meaning: A proud <part>flag bearer</part> leads the parade, but every year he slacks a bit more: first he drags the flag, then he sits, and this year he's lying face down in the <part>soil</part>, snoring. His marching has begun to <kanji>degenerate</kanji>.
堕.on: A <sound>du</sound>ck waddles over and pecks his ear to wake him.
堕.kun: His flag topples onto a parade float shaped like an <sound>o</sound>ctopus: to fall.

洪.meaning: At noon sharp, the whole town pulls the plugs on their bathtubs <part>together</part> for a world record. The <part>water drops</part> race down the drains, the pipes burst, and the high street turns into a river with rubber ducks bobbing past. The record is a <kanji>deluge</kanji>.
洪.on: A boy floats by on the giant ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne from the sweet shop sign.

慶.meaning: When the lost cat finally turns up, hiding in the garden <part>shed</part>, the whole family crowds in. Grandpa wraps it in a <part>blanket</part>, Grandma dances on a <part>folding chair</part>, and every <part>heart</part> bursts: pure <kanji>jubilation</kanji>.
慶.on: Someone runs to fetch a <sound>ca</sound>ke shaped like the cat.
慶.kun: They feast on <sound>yo</sound>gurt, set off a <sound>ro</sound>cket, and the cat naps on a <sound>co</sound>t.

寮.meaning: On the polar ice, a team of researchers builds one long <part>roof</part> over a <part>bonfire</part> and lays fifty sleeping bags round it in a ring. Everyone snores in turns and nobody's toes freeze. It's the warmest <kanji>dormitory</kanji> on the ice.
寮.on: A rival team calls their igloo a <sound>ryo</sound>kan, but nobody books a night there.

鍛.meaning: A young smith heats a bar of <part>gold</part> and climbs the stone stairs to her workshop, striking it once on each <part>grade</part> as she goes. One step, one blow, and by the top it's a gleaming crown. That's how she likes to <kanji>forge</kanji>.
鍛.on: Her workshop sits at the end of a dark <sound>tun</sound>nel inside the hill.
鍛.kun: She cools each crown in a bowl of <sound>ki</sound>wi juice, then eats a <sound>ta</sound>co to celebrate.

錬.meaning: At dawn, a goldsmith holds a ring of <part>gold</part> up to the window facing <part>east</part>, heats it in the first sunbeam, then plunges it into cold water. Hiss! Again and again, until it's tough as a nail: slow, patient <kanji>tempering</kanji>.
錬.on: A <sound>wren</sound> on the windowsill flinches at every hiss.
錬.kun: She hangs the finished rings in a <sound>ne</sound>t by the window to dry.

迅.meaning: A snail tired of being slow straps on a skateboard and shoots down a <part>ramp</part>, carving a wild <part>zigzag</part> through <part>ten</part> traffic cones. The crowd stares at its shiny trail: the slowest animal in the park is suddenly the most <kanji>swift</kanji>.
迅.on: Its secret fuel: one nibble of <sound>gin</sound>ger before every run.
